attrs.evidence: Both alternatives were tried in argument and refused. INV-R6.2 refused to rewrite the tree so that INV-R6.1 contained no R7 material, because that means deleting a concurrent agent's round and re-authoring it from the migration scripts of the party whose collision caused the problem — a receipt describing a transition no session performed. That refusal was right. What did not follow is that the mixed branch should stay canonical HEAD: those are not the only two options. INV-R8-RECOVERY starts from the INV-R6 commit in an isolated worktree, replays the reviewed content of INV-R6.1, the concurrent INV-R7 and INV-R6.2, and is promoted as a single child of INV-R6 under a revision id no quarantined receipt uses. The damaged branch is preserved unedited on refs/heads/invariant-quarantine. No fabricated intermediate transition is required, and the history says one true thing where it used to say two contradictory ones.
attrs.gap: The replay was performed and reviewed BY THE SAME EVALUATOR that implemented the round — mosaic/objectives.json §exteriority, unsatisfied for a fifth consecutive round. What makes this weaker than a clean history rather than equal to one: `INV-R8-RECOVERY.tree_delta` is derived from bytes and is exact, but WHICH of the mixed branch's changes were intended is a judgement, and the brief carries it in prose. The reviewed-versus-replayed correspondence is checkable only by reading ROUND8_RECOVERY_BRIEF.md against the quarantined artifact.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R6.2, §11. The version-control distinction between `revert` (a new commit that undoes) and `reset --hard` (a history that no longer contains the mistake).
attrs.statement: A damaged lineage is repaired by ONE new transition from the last verified-good ancestor that replays the reviewed content of the damaged branch under a fresh revision id — not by rewriting the damaged receipts and not by continuing from them.
